task.task_name: Triage a personal auto collision claim
task.task_description: You handle new auto insurance claims. A policyholder reports a two-car collision at an intersection and sends in their account of what happened, vehicle details, damage photos, the other driver's contact and insurance information, and a police report number. Some details might be missing or conflicting, and there may not be a repair estimate yet. Your task is to check the claim against the policy and available records, see whether there's enough information to move it forward, flag missing documents or possible coverage issues, and send it to the right claims team. Straightforward claims can go through the usual process. Claims involving injuries, conflicting accounts, signs of possible fraud, or complicated coverage questions need specialist attention. You're getting the claim ready for an adjuster, who will make the final coverage and liability decisions.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Review collision facts and available records
operational_subtasks.description: Review the policyholder’s account, vehicle and damage information, other driver details, and available police or claim records; compare the accounts and records for material inconsistencies or relevant incident facts.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assumption: this review occurs once per claim. Reviewing several submitted items and comparing them with available records takes moderate effort; availability and detail of records are not specified.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Check policy applicability and potential coverage issues
operational_subtasks.description: Compare the reported loss and available insured, vehicle, and driver details with the policy terms and status; identify apparent coverage concerns without making a final coverage decision.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assumption: a policy check occurs once per claim, with additional interpretation in an estimated 10–25% of claims involving a potential coverage complication. Comparing claim facts with policy terms requires focused review, especially when information or terms are unclear.

operational_subtasks.description: Check whether the information and documents needed to move the claim to adjuster handling are available; identify missing items or details, such as an estimate or report, when needed.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assumption: sufficiency is assessed once per claim; an estimated 20–50% of claims require identifying one or more gaps. The basic check is brief, while determining which missing items are needed adds effort in those cases.

operational_subtasks.description: Determine whether the claim involves injuries, conflicting accounts, indications of possible fraud, or complicated coverage questions that warrant specialist attention rather than the usual claims process.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assumption: the trigger screen occurs once per claim, with an estimated 10–25% requiring additional consideration of a possible specialist trigger. Routine screening is limited, while evaluating ambiguous indicators takes more effort.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Route and hand off the claim
operational_subtasks.description: Send the claim to the appropriate usual-process or specialist claims team, communicating the reviewed facts, potential coverage concerns, identified information gaps, and reason for specialist routing when applicable.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assumption: routing and handoff occur once per claim. Selecting the destination and conveying a concise claim summary is generally a brief activity, with modest added effort when specialist handling or unresolved gaps must be explained.
